<module id="JC_counter">
  <description>Implement a 64-bit Johnson counter (torsional ring counter), and the state of the similar 4-bit Johnson counter example is as follows: 0000, 1000, 1100, 1110, 1111, 0111, 0011, 0001, 0000.</description>
  <ports>
    <input id="clk" width_description="">Clock signal used for synchronous operation.</input>
    <input id="rst_n" width_description="">Active-low reset signal to initialize the counter.</input>
    <output id="Q" width_description="">64-bit register representing the current count value.</output>
  </ports>
  <logic_description>
    <description>
            Notice that below descriptions are along with tags  <logic />.
            With a  <logic type="combinational_logic" />, must construct this logic as interal wire declaration. Or this  <logic type="combinational_logic" /> can be declared as a `reg` but only be used in always(*) block.
            With a  <logic type="sequential_logic" />, must construct this logic as `reg` declaration. Must update this logic, in an always block, based on other  <logic type="sequential_logic" /> or  <logic type="combinational_logic" /> states.
            With a  <logic type="sequential_logic_operation" />, no declaration for this keyword. Just place this operation sequence in below mentioned description.
            With a  <logic type="combinational_logic_operation" />, no declaration for this keyword. Just based on the keyword `assign` to construct description of this combinational logic operation.
        </description>
    <logic id="Q_right_increament_shifting" width_description="" type="sequential_logic_operation">
        The current  <output refid="Q"> is a concatenation of 1-bit 1 and 63 bits [63:1] of  <logic refid="Q">.
        </logic>
    <logic id="Q_right_decreament_shifting" width_description="" type="sequential_logic_operation">
        The current  <output refid="Q"> is a concatenation of 1-bit 0 and 63 bits [63:1] of  <output refid="Q">.
        </logic>
  </logic_description>
  <implementation>On every rising edge of the clock signal (clk) or the falling edge of the reset signal (rst_n), the counter value is updated.
If the reset signal (rst_n) is low, indicating a reset condition, the counter value (Q) is set to 0.
Otherwise, if the least significant bit (Q[0]) is 0, the counter increments by shifting the current value `Q` based on `Q_right_increament_shifting`.
If the least significant bit (Q[0]) is 1, the counter decrements by shifting the current value based on `Q_right_decreament_shifting`.
</implementation>
  <task>Give me the complete Verilog code.</task>
</module>

module JC_counter(
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst_n,
    output reg [63:0] Q
);

    always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            Q <= 64'b0;
        end else begin
            if (Q[0] == 1'b0) begin
                Q <= {1'b1, Q[63:1]}; // Q_right_increament_shifting
            end else begin
                Q <= {1'b0, Q[63:1]}; // Q_right_decreament_shifting
            end
        end
    end

endmodule
